content.text:
**File:** `content/actions/reference/runners/self-hosted-runners.md`, section "Accessible domains by function" / "Communication with GitHub.com" (~lines 218-225).

Docs list the required domains for GHCR access as:
```
github.com
*.github.com
*.githubusercontent.com
ghcr.io
```
The doc then references a rule block named `domain-name-cname-recursive-firewall-rules` — the point being that `ghcr.io` resolves via CNAME to Azure/Fastly-backed CDN endpoints whose IPs change frequently. Your firewall must allow by **hostname/FQDN with recursive DNS resolution**, not by static IP — that's why locking to the specific `185.199.111.154` address breaks after DNS re-resolves to a different IP. There's no Docker daemon flag to "force" this; it must be handled at the firewall/proxy layer (allow the domain names above and let the firewall follow DNS resolution, e.g. via an FQDN-aware/DNS-based firewall rule rather than IP allowlisting).
